title: A Diagnosis Dilemma of Atypical Skull Base Osteomyelitis Mimicking Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
content: Skull base osteomyelitis is divided into typical skull base osteomyelitis and atypical skull base osteomyelitis (ASBO). The latter obtained its name due to the absence of temporal bone infection or otitis externa. Due to its vague clinical presentation, there is typically a delay in diagnosis and treatment of the condition. We report an immunocompromised lady with severe chronic headache, an unremarkable otoscopic examination with left nasopharyngeal mass mimicking nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Histopathological and radiological evaluation is imperative to attain the diagnosis of ASBO.
